claim: A GSPN is a directed graph of places and transitions whose arcs run only between a place and a transition (bipartite).
quote:
A PN comprises a set of places P, a set of transitions T, and a set of directed 
arcs A. In the graphical representation of PNs places are drawn as circles and 
transitions as bars. Arcs connect transitions to places and places to transitions.
locator: p. 93 printed (PDF p. 1), Sect. 1; GSPN 'as in (2)', p. 96 printed (PDF p. 4), Sect. 2
issue: The source never says 'bipartite'; it defines the PN with A a subset of (P x T) u (T x P) and the GSPN as a PN with two transition classes, which is bipartite in substance. Adversarial read: the definition is stated for the PN and inherited by the GSPN, not stated for the GSPN directly; holds.

claim: (uncited neighbour, leans on marsan1984) Tokens sit on places.
quote: Places may contain tokens, which are drawn as black dots.

claim: (uncited neighbour) A transition is enabled when each of its input places holds a token.
quote:
A transition is enabled when all of its input places contain 
at least one token.

claim: (uncited neighbour) Firing moves a token from each input place to each output place.
quote:
Enabled transitions can fire, thus removing one token from 
each input place and placing one token in each output place.

claim: (uncited neighbour) A timed transition fires after an exponentially distributed delay; its rate is one over the mean delay.
quote:
Timed transitions fire after a random, exponential|y 
distributed enabling time.
issue: Rate = 1/mean is a property of the exponential, not stated in this form; the source associates 'firing rates' with timed transitions on the same page. Fine for the reader.

claim: (uncited neighbour) An immediate transition fires in zero time and takes priority over timed ones.
quote:
If H comprises both immediate and timed transitions, 
then only immediate transitions can fire.

claim: (uncited neighbour) Of several enabled immediate transitions, one fires with probability proportional to its weight.
quote:
When H comprises several immediate transitions it is necessary to specify a 
proability density function on the set of enabled immediate transitions according 
to which the firing transition is selected.
issue: The 1984 paper selects by a specified switching distribution, not by weights normalised over the enabled set; the weight formulation is the later book's (marsan1995, cited in the next unit). Sentence is correct as a GSPN fact, but between the two cites the reader may attach it to marsan1984.
